hens_rule_text: Up to 4 small animals total (hens count toward this along with dogs 6 months or older, rabbits, ducks, etc.) allowed without a permit; more requires Department of Public Health approval.
permit_notes: No permit needed for the standard allowance of up to 4 hens; a permit from the Director of Public Health is needed to keep more, and the coop itself must be approved by that office.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 20 ft from any door or window of a residence.
coop_rules: Coop must be approved by the Department of Public Health; general sanitation and nuisance rules apply.
zoning_notes: Rules are in San Francisco Health Code Sec. 37, Keeping and feeding of small animals, poultry and game birds, and apply citywide rather than by zoning district.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: San Francisco Health Code Sec. 37, Keeping and Feeding of Small Animals, Poultry and Game Birds
BackYard Chickens forum, San Francisco California Chicken Ordinance

research_notes: The amlegal code page could not be opened directly (Cloudflare block, no Wayback copy available) so the figures rest on search-result extracts of Health Code Sec. 37 plus a secondary summary that agree with each other; the 4-animal combined cap and 20 ft door/window setback were not confirmed against the full code text.
